questions.question: The Indian Parliament comprises of the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President and the two Houses**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Parliament is a bicameral legislature consisting of the **President and the two Houses: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The President of India is an integral part of the Parliament, even though he/she is not a member of either House.
 
• **Lok Sabha** is the lower house of Parliament, also known as the House of the People.
 
• **Rajya Sabha** is the upper house of Parliament, also known as the Council of States.
 
• **Bicameral Legislature**
 
 
• It means the legislature is divided into two separate assemblies, chambers, or houses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha**

 
 
• Members are directly elected by the people of India.
 
• It has a maximum strength of 552 members.
 
• The tenure of Lok Sabha is 5 years.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha**
 
 
• Members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• It has a maximum strength of 250 members.
 
• It is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
 
 
• **President of India**
 
 
• The President is the head of the state and the supreme commander of the armed forces.
 
• The President has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament and to dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
• The President's role in the legislative process includes giving assent to bills passed by Parliament, issuing ordinances, and ensuring the smooth functioning of Parliament.

questions.question: What is the central theme of Poshan Pakhwada 2023, organized by the Ministry of Women and Child Development?

options.text: Millet - based foods for nutritional security

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Millet - based foods for nutritional security**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Millets** are rich in essential nutrients such as proteins, fibers, vitamins, and minerals, making them a vital component for nutritional security.
 
• The focus on millet-based foods aligns with the global trend towards sustainable and healthy diets.
 
• The initiative aims to address malnutrition and promote healthier eating habits, particularly in vulnerable communities.
 
• Millet cultivation is environmentally friendly, requiring less water and being more resilient to climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Millets** are a group of highly variable small-seeded grasses, widely grown around the world as cereal crops or grains for fodder and human food.
 
• They are known for their high nutritional value, being rich in dietary fiber, proteins, and essential minerals like iron, magnesium, and phosphorus.
 
• Common types of millets include pearl millet, finger millet, foxtail millet, and sorghum.
 
• Millets are considered a "superfood" due to their health benefits, including aiding in weight management, improving digestion, and reducing the risk of chronic diseases.
 
• **Nutritional Security** refers to consistent access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food that meets dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life.
 
• It involves not just the availability of food but also its affordability, cultural appropriateness, and nutritional quality.
 
• Ensuring nutritional security is crucial for preventing malnutrition and promoting overall health and wellbeing.
 
• **Poshan Pakhwada** is an initiative by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in India, aimed at promoting nutrition awareness and good practices for better health outcomes.
 
• It is part of the larger Poshan Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission), which seeks to improve nutritional outcomes for children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• The campaign includes various activities, such as community-based events, educational programs, and the distribution of nutritious food.
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture** involves farming practices that meet current food needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
 
• It emphasizes environmental health, economic profitability, and social and economic equity.
 
• Millet cultivation is considered sustainable due to its low water requirements and ability to grow in arid and semi-arid regions.

questions.question:
Read the following about Deficit reduction.

A. Government deficit can be reduced by an increase in taxes or reduction in expenditure.

B. In India, the government has been trying to increase tax revenue with greater reliance on direct taxes (indirect taxes are regressive in nature - they impact all income groups equally).

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deficit reduction** can be achieved by increasing taxes or reducing government expenditure.
 
• In India, there is a greater reliance on **direct taxes** to increase tax revenue, as **indirect taxes** are considered regressive.
 
• Indirect taxes impact all income groups equally, which can be burdensome for lower income groups.
 
• Direct taxes are considered more equitable as they are based on the ability to pay principle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government Deficit** refers to the difference between the government's expenditures and its revenues (excluding the money from borrowings). A high deficit can lead to higher public debt and interest payments, impacting the economy.
 
• **Direct Taxes** are taxes imposed directly on individuals and organizations (e.g., income tax, corporate tax). They are progressive in nature, meaning they increase with the increase in the taxpayer's ability to pay.
 
• **Indirect Taxes** are taxes imposed on goods and services (e.g., GST, VAT). They are regressive in nature as they are the same for all consumers, regardless of their ability to pay.
 
• **Fiscal Policy** refers to the use of government spending and tax policies to influence economic conditions. Deficit reduction is a key aspect of fiscal policy aimed at ensuring economic stability.

questions.question:
Read the following about Capital receipts.

A. All those receipts of the government which create liability or reduce financial assets are termed as capital receipts.

B. The main items of capital receipts are loans raised by the government from the public which are called market borrowings, borrowing by the government from the Reserve Bank and commercial banks and other financial institutions through the sale of treasury bills, loans received from foreign governments and international organisations, and recoveries of loans granted by the central government.

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital receipts** include all receipts that either create a liability or reduce assets.
 
• They are essential for financing the fiscal deficit of the government.
 
• Examples of capital receipts are loans raised by the government, borrowings from the Reserve Bank, and recoveries of loans granted by the central government.
 
• Capital receipts are different from revenue receipts which do not create liabilities or reduce financial assets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Receipts**

 
 
• Loans raised by the government: These include market borrowings, bonds, and loans from financial institutions.
 
• Borrowings from the Reserve Bank: This includes short-term and long-term borrowings.
 
• Loans from foreign governments and international organizations: These are usually obtained for specific projects or economic support.
 
• Recoveries of loans: These are repayments of loans previously granted by the government to states, public sector enterprises, or other entities.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts**
 
 
• Unlike capital receipts, revenue receipts do not create any liabilities or reduce financial assets.
 
• Examples include tax revenues (income tax, corporate tax, GST) and non-tax revenues (interest receipts, dividends, fees).
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**
 
 
• The fiscal deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts (excluding borrowings).
 
• Capital receipts are often used to bridge the fiscal deficit gap.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: How many triads were mentioned in Dobereiner's Triads?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dobereiner's Triads** were an early classification system in the history of the periodic table.
 
• Each triad consisted of three elements with similar properties.
 
• The atomic weight of the middle element in each triad was approximately the average of the atomic weights of the other two elements.
 
• Four known triads were proposed by Dobereiner:
 
 
• Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine
 
• Calcium, Strontium, Barium
 
• Sulfur, Selenium, Tellurium
 
• Lithium, Sodium, Potassium
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Dobereiner's Triads**

 
 
• **History:** Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner, a German chemist, proposed the concept of triads in 1829. It was one of the earliest attempts to classify elements based on their properties.
 
• **Significance:** Although only a few triads were identified, Dobereiner's work was significant because it highlighted the relationships between the properties of elements and their atomic weights, paving the way for the development of the periodic table.
 
• **Limitations:** Not all known elements at the time could be grouped into triads, and some triads did not fit perfectly into Dobereiner's rule.
 
 
 
• **Development of the Periodic Table**
 
 
• Following Dobereiner, other scientists like John Newlands and Dmitri Mendeleev made further advancements in the classification of elements, eventually leading to the modern periodic table.
 
• **John Newlands:** Proposed the Law of Octaves, which arranged elements in order of increasing atomic weights and noted that properties repeated every eighth element.
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev:** Created the first widely recognized periodic table, arranging elements by increasing atomic weight and leaving gaps for yet-to-be-discovered elements, predicting their properties.
tags: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.question: The city of _______ was located on Khadir Beyt (also spelled as Bet) in the Rann of Kutch, where there was fresh water and fertile soil.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dholavira**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dholavira** is one of the five largest Harappan sites and the most prominent archaeological site in India belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The site is located on **Khadir Beyt** in the Rann of Kutch, where there was fresh water and fertile soil, making it an ideal location for settlement.
 
• Dholavira is known for its sophisticated water conservation systems, including reservoirs and step wells.
 
• The site also features a unique layout with a citadel, middle town, and lower town, showcasing advanced urban planning.

questions.question: Which dance form from Karnataka involves large drums hung around the necks of men and is known for its religious and battle fervour?

• **Dollu Kunitha** is a popular drum dance of Karnataka, performed during various religious and cultural events.
 
• Dollu Kunitha involves large drums hung around the necks of men, creating a powerful and rhythmic performance.

• This dance form is associated with the worship of the deity Beereshwara or Beeralingeswara, a form of Lord Shiva.
 
• Performed primarily by the Kuruba community, it features elaborate drum patterns and vibrant costumes.

• **Table Tennis**

 
 
• Table tennis, also known as ping-pong, is a sport in which two or four players hit a lightweight ball back and forth across a table using small bats.
 
• The game takes place on a hard table divided by a net.
 
• Players must allow a ball played toward them to bounce once on their side of the table and must return it so that it bounces on the opposite side.
 
• Points are scored when a player fails to return the ball within the rules.
 
 
 
• **Arjuna Award**
 
 
• The Arjuna Award is a sports honor presented by the Government of India to recognize outstanding achievement in national sports.
 
• It was established in 1961 and includes a bronze statue of Arjuna, a certificate, ceremonial dress, and a cash prize.
 
 
 
• **Commonwealth Games**
 
 
• The Commonwealth Games is an international multi-sport event involving athletes from the Commonwealth of Nations.
 
• The event was first held in 1930, and since then it has taken place every four years.
 
• Table tennis is one of the sports included in the Commonwealth Games.
 
 
 
• **Asian Games**
 
 
• The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a continental multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The Games are recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and are the second largest multi-sport event after the Olympics.
 
• Table tennis has been a part of the Asian Games since 1958.
